notes.title: Weekly Update #128: Colour Customization
notes.content: [p]Hey all! Are you tired of the colour blue? Wish you could customize the colours of Crystal Horizons to your liking? Well, now you can! We've set up a new settings page to handle colour customization. You'll be able to set the colour used for each unit team in the game, as well as a colour for the overall user interface. Simply navigate to the settings page and select which colours you would like from a preset list.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44901040/47531d1317d93cedbc77ce7f970a6274aac5c7c2.png"][/img][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44901040/42f522c9517d258bda6dc558908c5a67a0ad1969.png"][/img][/p][p]Not everything is hooked up to the new system yet, but you can expect that almost everything will be affected by the colour you set. Of course, you can always just leave the colours at their default value, which would be my recommendation, but in my opinion it's better to have too many choices as opposed to too few. I've provided a couple of screenshots showcasing how the colours are applied so you can get an idea of how it would look.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44901040/5459434013da4fd6d080eb0225c7a64a6cc1ea49.png"][/img][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44901040/69de96c295af2ae889743a519cd39cd04d062a35.png"][/img][/p][p]Now, I've got one quick announcement to share. Throughout the month of October, we will be pausing the weekly updates so we can focus completely on finishing up some very important tasks. While the updates are awesome for sharing progress, having to have something prepared for every week has taken a lot of dev time over the years away from other more difficult tasks. It's great that we can show that we're still working actively on the game, but we need a little time to lock in without distractions.[/p][p]Next week's update (October 1st) will be the last update before the break. From then on, we'll be relatively quiet as we smash through our critical task backlog, before returning on November 5th. If all goes well, we should have some really cool things to share at that time, but we'll have to wait and see! Thanks for tuning in![/p]

notes.title: Weekly Update #124: Skill Selection and Target Preview
notes.content: [p]Hey all! Here's a first look at a new menu I've been working on. I've been doing a ton of research recently and have a bunch of new ideas for how to improve some aspects of Crystal Horizons, primarily focusing on the UI. Recently, I've been trying to improve the Action Menus, which are a little bit important seeing as they are your primary point of interaction in the game.[/p][p]Since the very beginning of the project, we've been using a design that involves small vertical menus that kind of fold out from the bottom right of the screen, pushing older submenus further left as you navigate through them. While there are some upsides to a layout like this, I constantly felt restricted when trying to convey information to the player. There's only so much space for information, and I cannot stress how important it is that a player has access to as much valuable information as possible as efficiently as possible.[/p][p]So, after a few failed attempts at making the old design work, I've moved on to a new layout. At this stage, we'll still be using the vertical menu for the first level of the action menu, which has options like Move, Attack, Skills and Items. I'm looking into something new for that too, but it isn't ready just yet. For options like Skills, previously we would open another vertical menu for skill categories (for example, Archer would have Archery, Elemental Quiver and Bow Arts as options), which would then open a third menu with all of the actual skills.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44901040/ad746b390269f7c627389a16bf6845a8825e06e8.png"][/img][/p][p]With this new design, however, I've managed to streamline the process into a single larger menu. Upon selecting Skills, you'll now open the Skill Menu, which has lists of skills just like before. Instead of being under different menus, requiring navigating back and forth through different levels, we now have other skill categories as separate tabs that can be accessed with a simple left or right input. Most importantly however, we're able to include a lot more information. I'm very excited about this, but nothing here excites me as much as the Target Preview.[/p][p]This little thing has been on my wishlist for years now, but I could never find a place for it that was both useful and easily accessible. Playtests have shown that attack range and area of effect are often some of the most confusing things for players to understand on a skill-by-skill basis. Now, when selecting a skill to use, you'll be able to get a strong idea of how the skill works without needing to select the skill and begin the targeting phase. This should make some of our more unique skills a bit less confusing to use.[/p][p]As always, we'll be looking to make small improvements here and there and clean up any errors. In fact, we've already made the panel a little bit smaller since we got the screenshots, but you'll have to wait until next week to see the difference. Additionally, we'll need to create some simple icons for the different skill categories, as right now I'm just reusing old status icons and the weapon icons. I'll be sitting on this one for a while and seeing what feedback I get and how it goes in tests, but I'm a big fan of the design personally so I have high hopes. Thanks as always for tuning in![/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44901040/16ea16aa14783a648c019c1c5d21035ca23ac57c.png"][/img][/p]

notes.title: Weekly Update #121: The Unit Circle
notes.content: [p]Hey all! This week, I'd like to share with you the first iteration of an addition I've wanted to implement for ages now. This is still an early draft version, like a proof-of-concept, but I have some cool ideas for how to improve it in the future. Introducing, the Unit Circle! Well, I'm calling it the Unit Circle, but it's not exactly a complete circle? I'm not really sure if that's the best name for it.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44901040/898687791527e47aa70cbc7c2d118aa3c5ea629b.png"][/img][/p][p]Anyway, if that name rings a bell then I'm shocked, but we initially mentioned 'Unit Circle' many updates ago. In that previous update, I shared with you all a look at some of our game settings. Among other items in the Visibility Settings submenu, we had options for the Unit Circle and the Unit Circle Intensity. As you can now see, the Unit Circle is a helpful guide to show which team a unit is on and which direction they are facing. It can help when looking at some of the more ambiguous sprites, like slimes for example.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44901040/7548e8b3890250b990c5c4b2f1c695f6017e9660.png"][/img][/p][p]Through the settings menu, you'll be able to set whether you would like them displayed at all times, displayed only when holding down the Tactical View button, or never. You'll also be able to adjust the intensity of the circle, which right now means adjusting how transparent the circle is. As I said before, I have some good improvements in mind for future iterations, but we'll have to wait and see! That's all for this week; thanks for tuning in![/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44901040/2c47d01c23b74fdb1c35de738f14342f05f60289.png"][/img][/p]

notes.title: Weekly Update #119: Status Border Adjustments
notes.content: [p]Hey all! Here's a quick look at some design changes we're trying out for status icons. First, we have a before-and-after comparison with the Ruptured icon (from Thief), where we've changed the background and background accent to be gradients rather than flat colors. It's a simple change, but a pretty impactful one in my opinion.[/p][p][/p][table equalcells="1" colwidth=","][tr][th][p]Before[/p][/th][th][p]After[/p][/th][/tr][tr][td][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44901040/0911ab27667457fb8e99b3ccdd8f2127bf375db2.png"][/img][/p][/td][td][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44901040/6a2d16ab457aff96457a5ae43201f6439c72c297.png"][/img][/p][/td][/tr][/table][p]The other change I want to highlight is the adjustment of the border used for the icons. As part of our goal to diversify our collection of UI assets, we spent some time identifying what works and doesn't work across Crystal Horizons so we can figure out where best to focus our efforts. In line with our findings, we're trying out a silver border for the icons to better match the rest of the UI.[/p][p]We've also slightly increased the size of the icons on the Unit Info Panel to better make use of the space and allow the details to display slightly better. Here you can see the previous version of Ruptured along with a collection of other icons that have had their border updated. Only Ruptured has had its background changed from this set, but the others will receive the same treatment over time.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44901040/71b89ad3a0dee0cbbce99f7da1be04661bbdde9d.png"][/img][/p][p]Depending on how we feel about the changes, we'll roll them out over time to all our existing icons. We also have a small selection of icons we're looking to redesign, so unless we make any other universal changes that will be our focus for the moment. That's all for this week though; thanks for tuning in![/p]

notes.title: Weekly Update #117: Progress Report - Mid 2025
notes.content: [p]Hey all! It's been a little while since our last big progress report, so I think now is a good time to share where we're at and what our priorities are for the next stage of development.[/p][p]To start with, here's a quick recap of what we've been up to since our last progress update:[/p][list][*][p]All main UI pieces (menus, windows, etc.) for the battle scene have had their layout updated and all but the Glossary are completely functional[/p][/*][*][p]Our eight beta classes have all their basic (non unique/skill) attack animations either completed or drafted and displaying in game[/p][/*][*][p]Additional revealed classes have class icons and base sprites either completed or drafted, but not attack animations[/p][/*][*][p]We've made some more battle maps, one of which we're showing off soon in another update after revealing it three weeks ago[/p][/*][/list][p]There's probably more, but those are the main things we've done recently. There's a few things that I've left out, and that's because I want to go into a bit more detail now.[/p][p]First off, status icons. We've shown off our status icons in a lot of weekly updates in the past. They are something that is usually pretty easy to get footage/screenshots of and talk about when compared to things like game systems, which is where a lot of our time goes. That said, some of the icons, especially the recently shown off Berserker icons for Shredded and Savagery, aren't quite up to standard.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44901040/9770873233f275c499c78ce49a74cf51ae7f1f0e.png"][/img][/p][p]Our overall lukewarm opinion of those icons led us to discuss and review all our icons and the artstyle we're using for them. As a result, we identified a number of weaknesses and possible improvements that could be made, and marked a not insignificant number of both old and new status icons for improvements. Our goal is to maintain the current artstyle while loosening up a bit on certain restrictions and improving overall quality. Once we're happy with the results, we'll share some before and after comparisons.[/p][p]This task should be relatively easy and not eat up too much development time in other areas, as it's something that can be done on its own at any time. I'll be working on it inbetween other major tasks.[/p][p]One of those major tasks is expanding our VFX systems. So far, all our visual effects have been made by hand using Unity's VFX Graph, but we've had to accept that we don't really have the skill and manpower to keep that up right now. As such, we're currently in the process of transitioning to pre-made visual effects, which we've acquired in great quantity and quality. The plan for now is to use these new effects where appropriate, and modify or create custom VFX for more specific skills.[/p][p]Whether we stick with the pre-made effects or eventually replace them all with custom effects isn't something we can decide right now. Once we have them working as intended in the battle scene, I'll share new gameplay videos with the new effects (and likely some other additional things we've done that haven't been seen since our last video). This is a task we've already started working on and are prioritizing right now.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44901040/c92e9fa3ea6c26f9b345176c054789d5859c9b4c.gif"][/img][/p][p]Finally, we have to address the lack of both UI and character art assets. As mentioned in the last update about the Glossary, we're currently too reliant on the few UI assets we have, and are looking into additional assets. I'd put this at medium priority right now; we definitely need to expand our options before progressing too much further. This task will require a lot of iteration though, so it might be a while before we have anything definitive to share.[/p][p]As for character art, I can't really say much more than 'we're working on it'. Our team lacks any professionally trained artists, and while we have been able to produce some character art in the past, we're painfully aware that the quality is lacking. On top of everything we're already doing, we're also training some members of our team in character art and are trying to reach a certain level of quality as quickly as possible. I'd love to say that we'll have something ready soon, but for now we'll have to wait and see.[/p][p]That's all I've got to share today. I want to genuinely thank everyone who's still with us throughout development. We're a small team working on this game as best we can in our spare time, and while I know development is painfully slow at times, I'm extremely grateful for your support. We'll keep doing our best to bring updates to you all, so thanks for tuning in![/p]

One of those major tasks is expanding our VFX systems. As such, we're currently in the process of transitioning to pre-made visual effects, which we've acquired in great quantity and quality. The plan for now is to use these new effects where appropriate, and modify or create custom VFX for more specific skills.

Finally, we have to address the lack of both UI and character art assets. As for character art, I can't really say much more than 'we're working on it'. On top of everything we're already doing, we're also training some members of our team in character art and are trying to reach a certain level of quality as quickly as possible. notes.title: Weekly Update #116: Glossary V2 - First Look
notes.content: [p]Hey all! We've made some pretty notable progress on updating the Glossary, the massive repository of information that can be accessed at any time. The screenshots I'll be sharing this week have been taken while the Glossary is in a state of 'not quite working right now', so while the layout is done it doesn't quite connect to the battle scene just yet. That will be the next step after making any further adjustments to overall layout, and then we'll get to add nice animations for opening, closing and navigating the Glossary.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44901040/57c77f4bc9a240706c1384991930f94fc30df2f8.png"][/img][/p][p]The first major change from the old Glossary is the introduction of a new landing screen. Previously, the glossary would open straight into a contents view which you would be able to scroll up and down through, but now we start on a simpler page with eight options to choose from. Most glossary entries will be sorted into the first five categories: Guide, Classes, Tiles, Items and World. The Skill Index and Status Index will provide A-Z lists of all skills or statuses in the game for quick navigation and reference, while the Recent category will provide a list of all entries that were recently made available.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44901040/06bcd42ec61df95bea08f244cd3bef3fabfa0b7f.png"][/img][/p][p]Upon selecting a category, we navigate to a view more reminiscent of the previous Glossary. We've adjusted the proportions and layout of the Glossary to be less overwhelming, and provided quick navigation buttons to other categories. Additionally, different entries might have slightly different layouts, such as statuses displaying their icons.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44901040/dee02945a13507a057bc1e0e560752ef497059e7.png"][/img][/p][p]Now, for the elephant in the room, I am aware that we have maybe three total unique assets in use here. If you didn't think we were overusing the blue gradient box asset before, then this should make it more clear than ever. We'll be spending some time in the near future diversifying our UI assets, so you can expect the design to change a bit once we've done that. Layout-wise, I'm pretty happy with how it looks, but it's definitely in need of some visual variety.[/p][p]That's all I've got for this week, though. Next time I show off the Glossary, it should be fully integrated into the game and have a greater variety of assets, so look forward to that! When it happens.[/p][p]Also, one quick announcement: Team Whirlwind unfortunately won't be exhibiting at AVCon this year. We're very behind on some of our goals (which I probably don't need to say) and decided that our time would be better spent working towards those instead of creating a new demo and doing all the fun preparation required for that and AVCon. Hopefully the beta will make up for that, so we're working full speed on everything needed to get there. Thanks as always for your support, and I'll keep you updated on that front![/p]

notes.title: Weekly Update #110: Tile Effect Icons
notes.content:
Hey all! Allow me to introduce a new addition to the Tile Panel in the top left; we now have custom icons for unique Tile Effects! Here we have Guard Aura, the passive defense buff granted by Knights, and Sanctified, a lingering healing effect placed by the Lumimancer's Sanctuary spell. While they are done in the same style as our status effect icons, they have a different shape to help them stay distinguishable.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44901040/0bb5f4001ba4aeda02a6a85e74a67c9d6e1849c5.png[/img]

There isn't really a limit to how many unique tile effects can be affecting a single tile at once, so I thought some icons would help break up the text and make it easier to recognize what's going on when lots of effects are in play. Originally, we did consider having visual effects on the tiles themselves, but that would add far too much visual clutter. As such, only active Tile Elements, like Burning and Steam, will have persistent visual effects. This way, players should be able to tell at a glance what elements they can cause reactions with, without getting confused by other active effects. That's all for this week!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44901040/1706e8a2ff27b55a7dd9e858d52964c33acc5d1f.png[/img]

notes.content:
Hey all! This week, let me share with you our latest addition to the battle scene. Tiles are on of the most important things in Crystal Horizons, with them each having their own Tile Element and any number of active Tile Effects. Currently, the Tile Panel in the top left of the screen shows the current Tile Element, the height value of the tile, and the name of any active Tile Effects.

You could always check the Glossary, but there's a much faster way to find out; simply hover over the UI element or open the Tile Panel as a menu using a dedicated key. In this state, you'll receive a list of all known reactions for the tile's current Tile Element, as well as detailed tooltips for any of the Tile Effects instead of the short ones you can see with the Tactical View key.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44901040/709fed02e5045db26d88e6f3ca434f42a8b39428.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44901040/5a9b6c9357dc725b7748157673d068cad07eda05.png[/img]

We've also adjusted the panel to now display both the base Tile Element and the current Tile Element, as certain reactions will reset the tile back to it's original state (such as the Smother reaction, caused by using Earth on a Burning tile). We've included in these screenshots the reaction legend for both Grass and Burning Tile Elements, showing most possible reactions in those states.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44901040/f4e78c5cb48d560ef0fc5f41a1096902a4a5361f.png[/img]

Similarly to entering the Tile Panel, we plan to also be able to go further into the reactions legend and have tooltips for each reaction, but that hasn't yet been implemented. That's all I've got for this week; thanks as always for tuning in!

notes.title: Weekly Update #101: Master Skills, Part 2
notes.content:
Hey all! This week is a follow-up to last week's introduction of Master Skills, going over some details I feel I missed or didn't explain enough. I'll also provide some insight into the concepting and creation of Master Skills.

The first thing I'll touch on is the Mastery gauge, the HUD element used to represent a unit's current Mastery resource. While it was visible in last week's clips, I didn't bring any attention to it, so I wanted to explain what the additional bar on the Unit Info Panel was and clear up an error I left in the clip (in the Seraphim clip where it appeared empty for a bit).

Once we figure out exactly how we want to lay it out, we'll likely add a numerical value like the other resource bars and breaks every 20%, to maintain parity with the Focus (FP) bar due to their interconnectivity. While we like the current design for the gauge, we might make further adjustments, as it was the final thing added before capturing the gameplay footage.

Now, where did the ideas for Master Skills come from, and why were they only revealed recently? Originally, many of our classes capped off their rank progression with a cool, powerful skill at Rank 10. Things like Knight's Heavensfall and Lumimancer's Radiant Ray; awesome skills to reward the player for sticking with a class all the way to the end, with great power and great resource costs as well. While these 'capstone' skills were cool in theory, in practice they interrupted the flow of gaining and spending FP too much, and weren't really satisfying to use.

That's not even mentioning the cost of remaining on a class already at max rank. We've made reclassing as simple and painless as possible to encourage players to build out a diverse array of options, and choosing to stay on a rank 10 class means not gaining rank EXP on another class, which might slow down acquisition of advanced classes (as a refresher, some classes require the unit have other classes at a certain rank or above in order to access).

So, we had all these amazing ideas for big, flashy skills, but they didn't fit into the gameplay loop cleanly on both a macro and micro level. That meant going back to the drawing board, figuring out if we could salvage these skills or if we would have to change them drastically. It was by looking at the core issue with FP that we began to iterate on our current solution; incorporate the skills into the core gameplay loop of building and spending FP.

Taking skills we previously intended to be powerful, end-of-progression things and making them available at rank 1 did require some changes to be made. In order to maintain the idea of providing a cool reward to the player for hitting max rank, the solution we came to was to have the skill increase in power at rank 10, meaning some skills were stripped back a bit at rank 1 before being upgraded back into their original concept at max rank. We also added an upgrade point at rank 5, both because rank 5 is a pretty important rank (for reasons which I'll discuss in a future update, maybe?) and so we could scale the skill up a bit more smoothly over all 10 ranks.

That's all I've got for now, though! I'm always happy to talk through some of our design intentions and processes (maybe a bit too happy, this was meant to be a short update). Closed beta test is still on the way, although I still can't give a definitive date. Development has been a lot more challenging than any of us expected, but we're as committed as ever, and I'll share any news I can when I can! Thanks for tuning in!

notes.title: Weekly Update #100: Master Skills
notes.content:
Hey all! Here it is, the big 100th update! We've been posting development updates for almost two whole years now, and I sometimes find myself looking back to see how far the project has come. Recent updates have been a bit slow, mostly various UI changes and the like. But now, it is my pleasure to introduce you all to a core game mechanic that we've been working on for a long time now: Master Skills!

Alongside Skills, Spells and Weaponskills, Master Skills are another type of activated ability, requiring their own resource to be built up before use. This resource, which we're calling Mastery at the moment, is built up by spending Focus (FP) at a one-to-one ratio. Using a Master Skill requires reaching 100% Mastery, and consumes the entire resource upon use. These skills are extremely powerful, limited by how few times per battle you'll get to use them; anywhere from 0-2 times depending on the length of the battle.

Due to the resource being gained by spending FP, this means that classes which generate and spend FP quicker will get to use their Master Skills more often. Similarly, classes that generate FP slower (such as spellcasters like Lumimancer and Pyromancer) will get to use theirs less. We've taken this into account and designed each class' Master Skill with the frequency of use in mind, leading slower classes to have generally stronger skills.

Each class gets access to only one Master Skill, available from Rank 1. At certain class ranks, the Master Skill receives slight enhancements, such as increasing range or adding an additional buff/debuff on hit. While most of the skills are still in development and unable to be shown off, I do have two I can talk about today: Lumimancer and Pyromancer! As spellcasters, they have skills which are both strong and awesome, so I figured there was no better way to introduce the mechanic than with some of the coolest!

[previewyoutube=jBiGeK2H4gM;full][/previewyoutube]

First, we have Lumimancer and the Seraphim skill! This skill creates a seraphic avatar out of light, which fires three devastating beams onto targeted areas! Much like Flash, the standard Lumimancer spell, this skill also deals damage to enemies while healing allies. While it does hit three times, it can only affect the same unit once per use, so dropping all three beams on one enemy will be pretty ineffective (it was really funny before we changed it though).

At later ranks, Seraphim gets upgraded to apply Illuminated to enemies. Since this skill can target up to 15 tiles under optimal conditions, it has the potential to be extremely strong, so we'll be keeping an eye on the power level. It also has a much longer range than other Lumimancer options, so its bound to find use when you need it most!

Pyromancer gets access to the destructive power of Worldrazer, a massive area-of-effect damage Master Skill. Worldrazer summons down a flaming meteor, dealing extreme damage in a huge area. Much like Pyromancer's other spells, the meteor does not care for whom it annihilates; ally or enemy alike. In the aftermath, expect the ground to be burned and barren having been Scorched, a tile effect that reduces incoming healing and deals damage upon movement through the tile.

Those who survive the impact will find themselves similarly burned, taking additional damage at the start of their turns. Worldrazer is truly a force of complete destruction, and is thankfully limited by the slow rate of FP generation that Pyromancer suffers from. At higher ranks, Worldrazer gains additional power based on how many stacks of Rings of Infernum the caster has, among other effects.

Alongside the skills being functional in-game, we've also made some improvements to our VFX systems and workflow; we're now able to animate a few more things, including the camera! Right now, we're using it primarily for Master Skills, to truly sell the scale and scope of the skill. I've included some early looks at the visual effects for both Seraphim and Worldrazer today, and while we wouldn't exactly say they're finished, I hope they can give you an idea of just how powerful these skills are meant to be.

Once we have a few more completed, I'll put together a video showcasing the Master Skills for our eight Beta classes, but until then I ask for your patience. Please look forward to more looks at these powerful skills in the future, and thanks for tuning in! 

(Showcase clips muted, haven't done sound effects yet. Apologies, please enjoy the VFX regardless!)

notes.title: Weekly Update #99: Maps Left Behind
notes.content:
Hey all! This week, I'm diving deep into the project files to look through some old maps we created! These were created using our Terrain to Map tool, which converts the heightmap of a Unity terrain to a map for Crystal Horizons, even including things like slopes! We've shown off this tool in action before, but today we're looking at some of the maps we made that didn't quite make the cut. These were made shortly after the creation of the conversion tool, while we were still seeing what it could do and testing its limits, so come with me on a little adventure across three different forgotten maps!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44901040/3e9db0b0e4e31df51e81716627982655f5b5dfbc.png[/img]

First up, we have this desert-like map. When maps are first generated, we give them two tile materials to use; one for tiles exposed to the air, like grass, and one to make up walls and other covered tiles, like dirt. Adding variance to the tiles comes a few steps later, so these maps didn't get that far, meaning they only have one or two tile textures on each. For this map, it means a lot of sand.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44901040/a594ec8b16ae2bcbc782a7eac2525f712abf741e.png[/img]

For the most part, the overall map is fine. The hill in the center and the valley that goes around it may be a bit too steep for interesting combat to take place, but with some adjustments it could definitely come back later down the line. Our second map today, however, is a bit more unique.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44901040/81b603998eb3d2055d038b23375b69566e965932.png[/img]

This flowery map has some interesting spires that dominate most of the map, with a plateau in the corner. With lots of high ground and cover, this could lead to some interesting interactions with ranged classes like Stormcaller and Archer, but there are some problems with it. Most notably, with single-tile raised areas like with the spires, it's possible for a unit to jump up and then be unable to be attacked by melee units due to the attack height limit.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44901040/c48410767f42faddf8b89c298b60990e588dc8ec.png[/img]

I suspect that this map was made primarily to test how sharp spikes in the terrain would behave with the conversion tool. Observing how the tiles ended up being placed, and how slopes were distributed, could have led to us having a better idea of how to create terrain to more accurately convert to the maps we wanted. I can see potential for this map, but it would likely need some major adjustments and a lot of playtesting to get to a good state.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44901040/e1a198abf3656afb54eebf60accb05a3ce6dab10.png[/img]

Now, our final map today is a big one. Easily the biggest one we've ever made, and a clear limit test for our conversion tool (and my poor PC). This mountain map is massive, and features a relatively linear path from down below, underneath a bridge, up a slope and then to the top layer of the map. Big maps with multiple layers are definitely things we wanted to try, but as we've learnt more about map size, enemy density and how combat actually plays out, it's become more and more difficult to justify designing a map like this.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44901040/efd4258c168dfaa162f92ec1c3407d7cebedc128.png[/img]

That's not to mention all the issues with visibility; we've got some tricks to make objects on the map less intrusive, but moving your units through a small space surrounded by walls would get very confusing, very fast. While this map is cool, especially owing to its scale, it's simply not a design that would lead to a fun, satisfying playable experience. Still, its sitting around in the project files, so maybe we'll find some way to use it in the future.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44901040/b5625a3c6e61ea7949316e18d13c595c4e611930.png[/img]

That'll be all for this week! Look forward to the next update; it's going to be a big one!

notes.title: Weekly Update #95: Class Design Insights, Part 2
notes.content:
This week will be a short continuation of last week's update, as I quickly go over some other class changes we're making. We focused on the Lumimancer class last time, but today I'm looking at Thief. It might not be surprising to see that the most notable adjustments are for our oldest classes, with newer designs like Enchanter and Berserker seeing minimal tweaks.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44901040/37b48d4dfc01ec67ca74f951220ea69e5b0c067c.png[/img]

So, to go back a bit, after AVCon we determined that Thief was in need of some gameplay updates. When the class was first designed, we wanted to focus on having a class that built up to dealing massive burst damage, stacking boosts over multiple turns and striking from weak points. To this end, the class was designed to function without a Move skill, having both Fade Out and Sharpen be standard skills.

In a vacuum, this didn't feel too bad, but when compared to other classes like Knight, Archer and Enchanter, not having a Move skill that tied into the class' rotation made it feel a lot slower, considering it's big damage attack only happened once every three turns. While we did discuss having a Move skill before AVCon, we were concerned about how strong it could be on a class with extremely high speed and decided to leave it until after testing.

Some of our discussions immediately following public playtests led us to the idea of adding in a Move skill that required certain conditions to use, but would allow Thief to reapply one of it's buffs. In a weekly update back in July, we mentioned how we were looking as allowing them to reapply Elusive, the critical damage multiplier and evasion buff, after landing a critical hit with a Dirty Fighting skill. After more iteration, here's what we're looking at now:

Two new skills have been added to the Thief's kit; the Move skill Tumble and the passive skill Unseen Strike. Tumble costs 20 FP, but allows the Thief to roll up to two tiles in any direction, even through enemies, but with a vertical movement of 0.5 tiles. Essentially, this means they can roll up and down slopes but can't jump within the movement. Using Tumble will apply Elusive for two turns, as opposed to the four granted by using Fade Out, but will allow the class to maintain a strong flow in battle.

Unseen Strike is a passive skill that grants the Unseen status to the Thief upon successfully hitting a Dirty Fighting skill from the correct positional. This status allows the Thief to use Tumble for 0 FP, essentially making it a free Move action. With this combination of skills, the class should be able to set up with Fade Out before getting within range of an enemy, then build FP with enhanced basic attacks, spend FP on Dirty Fighting skills, and roll to reapply Elusive for the enhanced critical damage and evasion. Tumble will be available on the class' base kit, while Unseen Strike will be unlocked at Rank 4.

There's been some other small changes to the kit in response to these additions, which we'll be watching carefully, and hopefully be able to show off in-game sooner rather than later. These last two updates have been walls of text, but next week I'll be sure to get some screenshots of some of the other things we've been working on in-engine. It's not ideal, but when we need an update every week, some of them have to be a bit less full than others. Still, I hope you're looking forward to trying out the updated classes, especially if you've played before! Thanks for tuning in!

notes.title: Weekly Update #94: Class Design Insights
notes.content:
Hey all! One of the things we're most confident in with Crystal Horizons, enough to name it as a core pillar of the game, is our class design. The complex, interconnected kits are unique among other games in the genre, taking inspiration from modern MMORPG design to elevate the identity of a class and add another layer of strategic decision making. I bring this up because I want to share the results of our playtesting and discussion regarding class kits, and highlight a few changes that we're testing with some classes.

We'll be focusing on Lumimancer today, but I might continue this with some of the other classes we've adjusted next week. Let's take a look at how the class started, our design philosophy for classes, and how we've evolved the class to where it is today.

Lumimancer is, at it's core, the primary healing class in Crystal Horizons. Other healing classes (not yet revealed but maybe soon?) may have certain restrictions on their healing such as range, area, or resource requirements. Unlike those classes, Lumimancer has a simple yet effective kit; Flash allows for ranged single-target healing or damage, Sacrament allows for ranged multi-target healing, and Rejuvenation grants a regeneration buff to allies in an area. Chuck in a few damage and utility spells as well and you have a solid, useful skillset that would be perfectly fine in a tactics game.

(Here's a side-by-side of the Lumimancer spell list, from one of our earliest builds next to current. Surprisingly, most spells have survived to the current iteration, although their effects have changed a lot.)

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44901040/ebe18f05818873c2ff4a59f95552ff8d33837790.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44901040/ce713ff3e80684ae3d5d3c05dfbed6e760312efe.png[/img]

Here in Crystal Horizons, though? That kind of simplicity simply doesn't fit alongside other classes on the field. Our intention is for players to be able to use their mastery of a class to set up and execute on complex strategies over multiple turns. To this end, we try to look at how well a class can act both reactively and proactively. Right now, our simple Lumimancer doesn't have much in the way of proactive gameplay, apart from applying regen and doing damage. So, how do we go about adjusting this base to be more in-line with our design goals?

The easiest way to do so is to introduce a status of some kind that allows different parts of the class to interact with each other. In this case, we have Illuminated. Illuminated is a debuff with a relatively simple purpose; be applied by some skills and consumed to power up others. Our first iteration of this had it be applied through area-of-effect spells (Luminous Impulse, Word of Law) and consumed by single-target spells (Flash, Judgement) to increase their damage.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44901040/6ea0b739f9161d13c36919e7e6c906d324e32ce4.gif[/img]

While the damage-dealing aspect of the class was now better, we also wanted to address healing. Healing often felt dissatisfying to do when compared to dealing damage, so we created the Blessing passive to bridge that gap. Now, any healing spells would additionally apply Blessed to healed allies, which granted them additional healing based on damage done by the Lumimancer that applied it. Now a Lumimancer can apply buffs and deal damage, apply regen and Blessed before damage is even taken, and keep allies healthy while still dealing damage.

This iteration of the class is what we brought to AVCon 2024, but there were still some pain points. Luminous Impulse was far too strong, being the correct choice for damage 90% of the time. Some skills such as Holy Ward were barely used, given the value that regeneration brought in comparison to a defense buff, and Flash was basically never used as people opted to use Luminous Impulse for damage and Sacrament for healing.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44901040/e79f00b9607175926df097527cb74ec4651c6275.gif[/img]

We want to shift the power around a bit without damaging the fantasy of the class; Luminous Impulse feels really good to use, and seeing massive damage numbers when Judgement hits an Illuminated target feels amazing. So, the changes we're currently testing involve weakening Luminous Impulse at base by lowering its damage and removing its ability to apply Illuminated. Instead, Flash will now apply Illuminated, alongside the more restrictive line AoE spell Word of Law, while Luminous Impulse, Judgement and Shining Jail will consume Illuminated to deal more damage (and extend the duration of Jailed for Shining Jail).

Illuminated now also increases accuracy against the affected unit, and allows the aforementioned spells to bypass accuracy checks when targeting Illuminated targets (guaranteeing they hit). This allows us to be a bit harsher on the base accuracy of Luminous Impulse and Judgement if we need to, giving us more ways to balance the spells once we get down to fine-tuning them. We also buffed Holy Ward, granting additional Block Rate (% chance to halve incoming damage) as well as defense.

We'll be testing these changes in the coming weeks, and you'll likely see some iteration of them when we hold the beta (soon). I know this is a pretty dense update, but I enjoyed talking through our design choices and the evolution of one of our most iconic classes. I had to leave a lot out, including a wide array of cut skills and spells, but I hope you enjoyed this inside look into how we iterate on our class design! Thanks for tuning in!

notes.title: Weekly Update #87: The Templar
notes.content:
Hey all! This week I wanted to make sure we showed off something completely new! While it's still very early in development, and I can only show you the sprite today, I wanted to reveal a new class. It's been a long time since our last reveal, and we've purposely not revealed anything for a while since we're still working on finishing up our 8 beta classes, but something new to spice things up never hurt anyone, right?

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44901040/07261e3a44e9c8052dc04b42f4a24522f4d1ee18.png[/img]

So, without further ado, allow me to introduce to you the Templar class! You can think of them as something between a Knight and a Lumimancer, but like every class in Crystal Horizons, Templars have their own unique gameplay style. Here's some quick info on the class:

Weapons: Sword, Greatsword
Armor: Heavy
Shield: Yes
Magic: Light, Healing
Brief Description: Highly adaptable frontline class with strong physical and magical defenses and decent strength. Has a number of skills and spells that are effective against magic users, such as inflicting Silence or draining MP. Can also provide support and some healing to allies.

Sounds pretty cool, right? I'm sure it would look even cooler, but I'm very limited in what I can show off today. Another notable facet of Templar is it's unlock condition: In order to reclass to Templar, the unit will require both Lumimancer at Rank 5 and Knight at Rank 3. This means that the unit will need to have gotten a decent amount of experience on both these classes before Templar is selectable. Many other classes also require prerequisite classes ranked up, so you won't have access to every class off the bat!

While both Lumimancer and Knight are required to unlock Templar, that doesn't mean that Templar is automatically the better option. All of our classes are designed to be as close to evenly balanced as possible, whether they are base classes or unlockables. Generally, we've tried to increase how specialised unlockable classes are, giving them more unique and potentially stronger options but making them more situational or difficult to maintain optimal performance on. We'll be watching very closely how these classes perform once players have their hands on them.

Speaking of which, Templar (and Occultist, who we've introduced before) will not be a playable class in the (still) upcoming closed beta. We're committed to making our selection of 8 classes for the beta as complete as we need for the data to be valuable. However, this is the tenth class we've officially revealed for Crystal Horizons, so that's a great milestone! We have a few more classes cooking behind the scenes, but we'll likely keep those under wraps a while longer. With that, I'll sign off. Thanks for tuning in, see you next week!

notes.title: Weekly Update #85: Elemental Reactions
notes.content:
Hey all! It's time I talked a little bit about a system we've mentioned here and there many times, and one we are considering one of the strongest hooks of Crystal Horizons: Elemental Reactions! We've been quiet on this one for a variety of reasons, and I still can't share too much right now, but I can share some screenshots and a brief introduction to the mechanic.

So, the name sounds pretty self-explanatory, but an Elemental Reaction occurs when a specific element is applied to a tile. Usually, this is through a skill or spell, or maybe a specific item. Let's use Pyromancer's Blaze spell as an example: This spell deals Fire damage in a plus-shaped area. Not only does this deal damage to any units within the area, it also applies the Fire element to all the tiles within the area.

Now that we have our applied element, which we call the catalyst, we check to see if the tile's current state has any possible reactions from a fire catalyst. For a Grass tile, we get the Burn reaction, which sets the tile alight with flame, which I'm sure many of you are familiar with already. Along with changing the tile state, the reaction will also affect nearby units in some way, like dealing damage or applying a status effect. Today, I'll be briefly introducing two new possible reactions, and talking about further reactions that can be performed from them.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44901040/9124f1310b954b57691ac0c692260614e3fba668.png[/img]

First, applying the Earth element to a Stone tile will scatter sharp stones around the tile, changing the tile state to Rocky. Similar to Burning, this tile state will deal damage units, but rather than dealing damage at the start of their turn it will instead deal an amount of damage when walking onto the tile. This means the damage can add up pretty fast if a unit walks through a bunch of Rocky tiles all at once.

Further applying the Lightning element to a Rocky tile performs a Magnetize reaction, changing the tile state to Magnastones. These are much more potent than the rocks from Rocky, and offer some additional powerful reactions. I won't reveal what these reactions are today; we want there to be some sense of discovery as players experiment with different elements, but I will say that any reactions from Magnastones will reset the tile state. We've tried to design our reaction trees to be engaging and rewarding, but not too complex or so powerful as to become the dominant strategy.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44901040/bb5a28a89b8abd746e32d0e548a8140b96d84aba.png[/img]

The other reaction I'll touch on today is Steam. This one can be achieved in two different ways; applying Fire to a Water tile, or applying Water to a Burning tile. On reaction, units on the reacting tile and adjacent tiles will take some Fire damage, and a steam cloud will be created on the reacting tile. This Steam will block line-of-sight, required for some actions, and can be further reacted upon.

From Steam, applying the Ice element will perform a Crystallize reaction, dealing Ice damage to any unit on the tile and changing the tile state to Ice Crystals. Like Magnastones, I can't go into more detail right now, but I hope you all look forward to playing around with elemental reactions when you get your hands on Crystal Horizons! We've put a massive amount of time and effort into designing the different paths you can go down with reactions, and hope finding them all will be a super fun experience! Thanks for tuning in!

notes.title: Weekly Update #83: Settings and Customizability
notes.content:
Hey all! Depending on who you ask, the Settings menu can be one of the most important things to get right when making a game. Who doesn't know someone who jumps right into the settings menu to tweak everything seconds after launching a new game? While it may not be one of the most glamourous things to show off in a weekly update, it's still a crucial part of the overall experience.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44901040/ab57c30f3d98f1cdcc1ef970fabaf755fb69d8a8.png[/img]

I'm pleased to show you an in-dev implementation of our new Pause Menu and Settings Menu. There's still a number of settings that haven't yet been implemented, and we're still creating more assets to spruce the overall design up a bit more, but I hope this is still a good look at some of the things we've included as adjustable settings.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44901040/2d78e7871b6c8680335654828c88b839c0c437e3.png[/img]

Our Display and Audio settings are relatively standard as far as things go, but I'd like to talk a little bit about things found in our Gameplay and Visibility categories. Under Gameplay, our first setting determines what happens once the turn of a unit under the player's control begins. Currently, the cursor jumps to the new unit, and remains on the map. With this setting, it can instead immediately open the first level of the Action Menu, cutting out an initial button press. We've had some feedback on this and wanted to make sure we implemented it, so here it is! We also have settings to change which direction is north for the Grid Cursor, as well as the speed the cursor moves when holding a direction or using an analog stick (the Free Cursor).

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44901040/6a845be65b2dcdd79ada44240920f00b0a1c7c0c.png[/img]

Under Visibility, we have a selection of handy toggleable settings that players can tune to their liking. Visual aids like a grid overlay and permanent team-coloured outlines can help mitigate confusion while playing, but can also add to the visual clutter at times, so we give players the choice of how they want these to be accessed. Tactical View is a mechanic that's been in Crystal Horizons for a long time, but I just came up with a cool name for it recently. By holding the Tactical View button, you can see unit health bars, expanded information on the Tile Info Panel, and whatever else you choose to toggle on in Visibility settings!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44901040/7548e8b3890250b990c5c4b2f1c695f6017e9660.png[/img]

I might be able to show you what some of those settings look like soon, but we're still working on them, so hang tight! Thanks as always for tuning in, and I'll see you next week!

notes.title: Weekly Update #74: Deploying Units and Beta Update
notes.content:
Hey all! Here's a look at a screen you'll be getting very familiar with while playing Crystal Horizons: The Deploy Units menu! Accessed from the Deployment Phase top menu, here you'll find a list of all the units in your crew that you can deploy onto a battle map. You'll be able to quickly reference their level, rank and equipped weapons and armor, as well as view their stats and inventory. Today I'm sharing a quick screenshot with some almost-final assets; this is one of the last pieces of UI required for the closed beta, so we're still making some adjustments to the colors and sprites.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44901040/15b6e5935078586103ade94e536310bfe49aeba3.png[/img]

This also serves as a nice way to show off all our revealed classes so far (with their class icons), with Crow as a Thief and Chieri as a Lumimancer. While these two are the only named characters right now, there will be a number of other unique characters you can deploy as well. We've not revealed them just yet, but you'll likely get some information on them sometime after the beta.

Now, speaking of the closed beta, I thought now would be a good time to give a more in-depth update on where we're at with getting that ready. Initially, we were aiming for late August to hold the beta test. As you may know, it is currently late August, and we have not yet held the beta test. Let me go into detail on how things have been going.

Currently, there are a small number of things that we're working hard on finishing, or problems we're resolving. For our classes, five out of eight classes are currently feature-complete. Thief, Stormcaller and Berserker are currently still receiving updates, with Berserker being the furthest behind. We don't expect finishing up these classes to take too long, but there's a number of issues that need to be addressed before some of the more complex features of these classes can be created and tested.

Outside of bug fixes and class development, the other thing we're currently behind on is portraits. Some of our class portraits, like Knight and Pyromancer, are over a year old. The artstyle and ability of our sole character artist has evolved quite a bit from then, so not only do new classes need portraits, but a large number of old classes also need remade portraits. This issue isn't critical for the closed beta, but is required for pressing things like updated screenshots and (importantly) a game trailer.

Outside of those two areas, most things are ready for the closed beta. Music, sound effects and visual effects are either finalized or in their final update pass, the sprites are looking as good as ever, and animations are also in the finishing stages. The Glossary is being steadily filled out, and unless there's some game-breaking issue discovered, it should be fully accessible during the beta test. We're tuning the UI a bit all over the place, but overall we're happy with where it's at.

So, when can we expect the beta? Assuming all goes well, sometime during September. I can't give a date in confidence, as we're making some big changes to systems and I don't know how many bugs will pop up, or how long it will take to fully integrate into the game. In terms of portraits, Stormcaller and Berserker need their portraits finished, but otherwise we can continue using the older portraits for the beta test, so we won't need to hold back for that. We're giving our all to make sure everything is ready for you all, so I ask for just a bit more patience! Thanks for tuning in, I'll see you next week!

notes.title: Weekly Update #73: Elemental Resistances?
notes.content:
Hey all! This week, I wanted to talk about another game mechanic we've not touched on much yet. Elemental Resistances provide percentage-based modifiers to incoming damage when that damage is of a specific element. This can either increase or decrease the amount of damage taken depending on the attack used. Classes in Crystal Horizons have their own Elemental Resistance modifiers, which are applied to the unit additively when that class is selected.

For an example, in some of our previous updates we've shows off the Reclass window, where relevant stats for each class are displayed. For the sake of convenience, I'll take a screenshot from a previous update, showing Lumimancer's stats at Level 10. Lumimancers receive 20% less damage from Light aspected attacks, such as other Lumimancer spells or an Archer with Light Arrows, but are vulnerable to the Dark element due to their -15% value. In the screenshot, the class also has a 5% resistance to some other elements, but we have since removed that due to some class design frameworks I'll talk about shortly.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44901040/5ead1849d8e7016419d4753e19ebff2fb72821b7.png[/img]

In terms of how total Elemental Resistance is calculated, we assume that the base unit has a 0% value in all elements. The Elemental Resistance values from the class are then added directly to those values. Equipment is then calculated and applied, and then finally any relevant status effects are applied. We're still working out exactly how we want to apply equipment and status resistances, whether that's additive or multiplicative; further testing should help us decide exactly how we want to handle it, or if we want to make any other changes to the formula.

Now, to follow up on those class design frameworks I mentioned earlier. Internally, we categorize our classes into one of five categories depending on their skills, stats, weapon availability and expected playstyle. These categories will likely not be relevant for the game itself, and are expected to be used solely for our own organisational benefit. The five categories we use are as follows: Tank, Melee Martial, Ranged Martial, Full Caster and Partial Caster. I'll briefly touch on each category and talk about where each of our revealed classes fit right now.

Tanks are designed with high survivability first, and often feature skills that allow them to control the battlefield effectively. Knight is the only class we've revealed in this category, and is the reason why I've brought this topic up in an update about Elemental Resistances. In order to help with their expected playstyle, classes in this category have the highest total Elemental Resistance across all elements. We decided that the weak multi-resist would be something exclusive to Tanks (mostly), so removed it from the classes that otherwise had it.

Melee Martial classes include Thief and Berserker; classes that primarily deal physical damage with melee weapons. Ranged Martial classes are similar, but trade some raw power for attack range. Archer is the only revealed Ranged Martial class so far. The main distinctions between Full Casters and Partial Casters are whether or not the class has the Staff weapon, and how reliant they are on casting spells and consuming MP. Lumimancer, Pyromancer and Stormcaller are considered Full Casters for this reason. Stormcaller is a unique case, as the other two are Staff only, but Stormcaller can also use Bows. Despite this, the class is still designed to primarily use spells, and have class skills that alter the functionality of Bows to achieve this.

Partial Casters are the most broad role. These are classes that utilize both physical damage and magical damage, both skills and spells. Unlike Full Casters, these classes cannot use Staves, and therefore are unable to access Staff weaponskills to recover MP or augment spell properties. Instead, these classes are expected to utilize basic attacks, weaponskills, FP-spending skills and MP-spending spells in order to balance their resource consumption and generation. Some of our most complex class designs fall into this role, including Enchanter and Occultist.

I've been very brief with my explanations here, but I primarily wanted to talk about the distribution of resistances across these categories. Tanks generally have the most resistances, Full Casters and Partial Casters have strong resistances to elements that their spells cover, and Melee Martial and Ranged Martial classes have few to no base resistances, but also no weaknesses. This doesn't account for class skills or equipment, however. While this system may make some classes weaker in some scenarios, most spellcasters have access to more than one damaging element and should be able to work around bad matchups.

I'll stop there for today; progress on getting the Closed Beta ready is going well, I'll share more info next week as we come closer to the date we initially projected. With that, thanks for tuning in, and see you next week!

notes.title: Weekly Update #70: HUD Improvements
notes.content:
Hey all! We're getting very close to the closed beta now, so while the team is hard at work finalising assets and stomping bugs, we've had time to improve some of the UI a bit more! There's a bunch of small changes here and there, but what I'd like to bring to your attention this week is both the addition of some new fonts, and a rework of the Floating Text system!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44901040/c7abcef6351429e1c3df1d9730fe5eec3c4a57a4.png[/img]

We've gone and picked out some fonts to help spice up the visuals a little bit, as well as improve readability across the HUD. I don't really have a lot I can go into detail with here, but we're feeling pretty good about the choices and think they're really helping to make the menus pop.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44901040/087ec447554f831c7fa7a9144d17edebbe2be50c.png[/img]

We've also reworked Floating Text, which is the text that appears over a unit when something happens to them. This is usually damage numbers, or statuses being applied or removed. Previously, the text would spawn, do a quick fade-in, float upwards and then fade out. This was fine, it was functional, but it could get quite busy and difficult to parse at times.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44901040/6ea0b739f9161d13c36919e7e6c906d324e32ce4.gif[/img]

With the rework, we now have the text appear much faster, and have it hover at a set position above the unit. If multiple instances of floating text are spawned at once on the same unit, then we push previous text further up to make room above the unit, ensuring that the application of multiple statuses is much less confusing. I've captured a short clip of nine instances of floating text appearing at once, and while we're still looking to improve readability when multiple units have floating text in front of another, we feel it's already made a massive improvement.

Now I'm sure you're all waiting patiently for the closed beta to kick off, and while I'm still not able to give you an exact date, I can say this much: We are currently expecting the closed beta to start mid-late August! There's still a lot to finish up, but we're currently aiming for a date within that range, and will let you know immediately if it needs to get pushed back a bit. Thanks for tuning in!

notes.title: Weekly Update #66: AVCon Class Performance Review
notes.content:
Hey all! This week, I've got a bit of a look back at how each class in the AVCon build has been performing, and what we might be looking at in the future for them. Huge thanks to all who gave Crystal Horizons a shot over the weekend; we got heaps of feedback and are already in discussions for what direction the game should head from here.

To start with, [b]Knight[/b] performed as consistently as always, taking plenty of damage and striking back with powerful basic attacks. We're overall satisfied with how the class felt to play, and how intuitive Active Defense is. We may look at some changes to the order at which they acquire skills, but don't have any major plans to change it at this stage.

[b]Lumimancer[/b] was given a few more tools this time around, including the Blessing passive (Healing an ally grants Blessed, granting them additional healing whenever the Lumimancer deals Light damage to an enemy). This ability allowed players to perform a quick heal on an ally in danger, then continue dealing damage while passively healing the ally further, which made the class feel more fluid than before. The real star, however, was Judgement, a new single-target damage spell. Despite it's extreme MP cost, players still ended up using it a lot, draining the class of it's MP very quickly. Our intention was for Judgement to be used with the critical damage bonus from the Illuminated status, while Flash was used as a cheaper damage spell, so we may look into better communicating this or making some changes to the skill.

[b]Enchanter[/b] made it's debut performance here, and results were all over the place. Due to it's expansive kit, we saw many ways the class could be played. Some players used it as a buff-bot, ensuring the rest of their team had haste, regen and lifesteal as often as possible. Some played it as a pure spellcaster, using Aspected Spark and Aspected Flare almost exclusively. The few times we did see a player interacting with the Cut and Tie mechanic, the class performed extremely well, so we're mostly just looking at improving communication for the class at this stage.

[b]Thief[/b] unfortunately was lacking in this build. While the class does have the highest potential damage in the game right now, it does not feel particularly good to spend two turns just applying buffs and then doing a massive backstab. We also saw very few players interact with the Dirty Fighting skills, which are meant to be a core aspect of the class, inflicting debilitating debuffs.

I'll go on a brief tangent here to talk about Move skills. Initially, these skills, which consume the unit's movement for the turn instead of their standard action, were granted only to a focused selection of classes. Knight's Active Defense and Pyromancer's Invocation were originally designed as Move skills, as both classes are incentivized to not move for various reasons. Elemental shift skills on Archer and Enchanter were later changed from standard actions to Move actions, as the class flowed significantly better when they didn't have to spend a turn not dealing damage to switch element.

As the game has developed, we've come to appreciate Move skills as tools to massively increase the fluidity of classes, and have been implementing them on more classes to great success. Lumimancer, and other classes that wield the Staff weapon, have access to the Staff Weaponskills list which include a number of Move skills. Thief, however, we were initially very reluctant to grant a Move skill to, as the class was carefully designed and calculated to function using purely standard actions.

Recent playtests have shown us that Thief has some issues, and can be one of the less engaging classes to use. We're still early in on concepts for this, but we're looking at giving it a unique Move skill that helps blend their Dirty Fighting skills into their setup and burst backstab combo. The current damage combo involves using Fade Out to gain Elusive, increasing Critical damage, using Sharpen to empower the next basic attack, and then attacking the enemy from the rear to do tons of damage. While dealing over 100 damage in a single hit feels good, the setup turns are boring, and the class isn't interacting with the powerful debuffs applied by Rending Slash and Rupturing Strike.

Our current plan is to grant Thief access to a Move skill that can be used only after executing a Critical hit with a Dirty Fighting skill. Using this Move skill will allow the Thief to move while applying Elusive, at a shorter duration than using Fade Out. This change should allow the class to deftly weave between setting up for backstabs and applying powerful debuffs when needed. We're still working out the details, but feel pretty good about this direction for the class.

This post ended up being pretty long, so I'll stop here for today. Our next upcoming goal is the Closed Beta, invites to which will be offered to members of our Discord server! I can't give a definite time on when that will be, but we're working extremely hard to get it all ready. I'll keep you posted in future updates; until then, thanks for tuning in!

For this update, I'd like to introduce (or reintroduce?) a character from the game. We've featured Lumi in many updates, as well as taking center stage in our key art. Now though, we finally have a name and some full-body art: Meet Chieri, a Lumimancer who joined the crew of the Black Duke shortly before Crow, the player character. Here's a short introduction to her now:

Chieri was born in a region far from where the story of Crystal Horizons takes place. After displaying high magical aptitude at a young age, her parents placed her in the care of the Adgai Duchy's church and she was relocated across the skies. Training as a Lumimancer, Chieri studied diligently and graduated with great results. This gave her the privilege to continue training and become a Templar, a holy knight in service of the Duke, but she refused.

Far more than status or glory, Chieri craved adventure. Being able to soar across the skies and offer succor to those she came across was her true calling. Leaving behind the Adgai Duchy which she called home for over a decade, Chieri took a ferry across the clouds and began her travels.

Some time later, Chieri encountered the airship Black Duke and it's crew, who shared with her their philosophy: They never harm or steal from the innocent or weak. The ideals of the odd crew resonated with Chieri, so she joined their adventures as a Lumimancer and medic. In her time as a sky pirate she has proven herself as both a reliable healer and warm friend, and makes sure to enjoy every second of her adventures across Sazdemir.

We're super happy to finally be able to drop our first full character art, as well as giving a name to Lumi. Chieri will be one of a small number of crew members with a unique design and gameplay applications. What those applications may be, I'll have to save for another time. That's all I've got for now though; thanks for tuning in, and I'll see you all next week!

notes.title: Weekly Update #51: Class Skills vs. Weaponskills!
notes.content:
Hey all! This week, I'm going to talk about Class Skills and Weaponskills, how they differ, and provide some insight into our design philosophy for the two.

Both classes and weapons gain EXP through use, and gaining enough EXP will cause a Rank Up. Class Ranks begin at Rank 0, and finish at Rank 10. Weapons instead start at Rank E, and end at Rank S. At each Rank Up, the unit will gain an additional Skill which they can utilize on that class, or when that weapon is equipped. Weapons always give an active skill that can be used in combat, but classes may grant a passive skill instead of an active skill.

A notable upside to this system is that it allows units to maintain a level of power as they change classes. As an example, let's say we have a unit who has just reached Rank 10 on Knight (access to Sword, Greatsword, Spear). While leveling the class, the unit used primarily Greatswords. Upon reclassing to Berserker (access to Greatsword, Axe), they will not be able to utilize their Knight Class Skills, but can choose to equip Greatswords and retain access to their unlocked Weaponskills. Alternatively, they could choose to use Axe, and begin gaining experience and ranks in that weapon type, which could then be transferred to Occultist (Axe, Dagger).

Due to this accessibility, we design Weaponskills to be relatively simple. Some may simply be higher power attacks that cost FP, some may apply a debuff, and some may have additional range or area-of-effect. The number of active skills can vary wildly between classes, especially when spellcasting classes get involved, so some classes appreciate the additional options Weaponskills provide much more than others.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44901040/e5363590d44948583ac4bc0ddab4ff78be4c0496.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44901040/62a425ed601e64aa9ab0a3636b48862a3f4b5921.png[/img]

The outlier to our Weaponskill design practices is Staff. While many classes in the game have access to spells and magical effects, the Staff weapon is granted to a carefully curated set of classes due to it's power. Stormcaller has access to both Staff and Bow, but Lumimancer and Pyromancer can use only Staff. This is an intended balance decision, meant to solidify these classes as dedicated magic casters. Stormcaller is unique among them with access to Bow, but certain passive skills on the class cause the Bow to function differently to address the power imbalance between the weapons.

Staff users begin with Spirit Align at Rank E, which grants them the unique ability to sustain their MP for much longer periods. All other ranks of Staff grant a Move skill that augments the next cast spell, such as increasing it's range, it's power and cost, or it's action speed.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44901040/88476b549ff3d11c6b7269f33cd2e3fdb48ac4d0.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44901040/0e3c3a5e937d6726796db413f9d0408480550378.png[/img]

Class Skills, meanwhile, are heavily focused on establishing a core identity, gameplay mechanic, or theme, and expanding upon those things as the class ranks up. I'll borrow Knight again for this example. Knight's core gameplay revolves around maintaining the Knight Oath buff, blocking damage to attain Element Loaded, and being a tank that is difficult to remove from the field. At Rank 0, or Start, Knight has access to the bare essentials for this identity to work, including the Knight Oath skill, Active Defense to guarantee block chance, and Guard Aura to provide protection to allies.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44901040/25acc79869b25cde10b847a997150f196118d7fc.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44901040/a02b2fe9b7fd026c1f98aabe6af24e4dd1c6cc03.png[/img]

As Knight ranks up, it gains skills such as an auto-cast Knight Oath on the first turn of combat, the Binding Strike skill which prevents enemy movement, and various additional effects stacked onto Knight Oath. It also gains the ability to keep Element Loaded when using the single-target Elemental Discharge, instead of losing it after using the skill. As the skillset improves, we try to ensure that each additional skill does something to reinforce the identity of the class. Weaponskills allow us to commit to this direction, ensuring all classes still have access to generically useful skills.

I could go on with more examples, but I would like to wait until we have better in-game infrastructure to make skill progression easier to visualize. That's all I've got this week; see you all in the next update!

Stormcaller is unique among them with access to Bow, but certain passive skills on the class cause the Bow to function differently to address the power imbalance between the weapons.

notes.title: Weekly Update #50 - Deployment Phase and Improved Menus!
notes.content:
This week, I've got two new screenshots; a first look at the Deployment Phase and a change we've made to the Action Menus! At the beginning of a battle, you will enter the Deployment Phase, in which you can choose which units you'll be deploying for the map. You can also view the map to take a look at enemy information, or manage items and classes through the Crew menu. This is still an early version, so it might look vastly different the next time you see it!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44901040/df72286dcdfc4e268cc8581e494af0a6346dfb2b.png[/img]

Second, we've restructured the Action Menus to be more vertically compact, and eliminate the problem of some classes having way too many skills for a single menu to reasonably hold (especially since they can only display five elements at once right now). Now, the top level will always include Move, Attack, Skills, Items and End Turn. Under Skills, we now have the previously top-level skill categories, such as Magic Weaving and Conceptualization, or Thief's Thievery and Dirty Fighting.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44901040/38b651371cd7c47ee947769a585126d1f804e8ae.png[/img]

The Action Menu can now expand once more for a total of three menus. We've been on the fence about making this change in the past, but with the implementation of Items coming closer we've realized that in order to structure the Items menu in a good way we'll need three menus. With that, we decided to change up Skills at the same time.

Finally, in the same screenshot I have most of the Sword Weaponskills visible. We're a bit short on icons, so please forgive the overuse of the red sword for now. As a quick refresher, weapon ranks are different to class ranks, so a character that gains ranks in Sword while classed as Knight can carry over those ranks and skills when classed as Enchanter. Weaponskills are a bit simpler than class skills, due to their wide availability, but offer a variety of additional options for classes.

That's all I've got for you this week; thanks for tuning in, and I'll be back next week with more updates!

notes.title: Weekly Update #49: Glossary Preview
notes.content:
This week, I'll be showing off an early version of the in-game Glossary, one of the things we're investing heavily into as part of our mission to make as much information available to the players as possible! 

The Glossary can be accessed at any time during gameplay with a single button press, and depending on where you press that button you can be brought to the top level, or directly to an entry that you're hovering through the Unit Window or Action Menu! This will allow you to quickly query the specifics of a skill or effect, should the information on the immediate HUD not be enough for your current needs.

Much of Crystal Horizons is internally powered through the Glossary; most UI-accessible information is stored within it. We expect that this resource will prove invaluable for new players and veterans of the genre alike, especially in regards to the specifics of how our classes work.

Here's some screenshots of the Glossary in-engine, showing some of the information that will be available. This is still early in development, so some aspects are not yet functional, and most entries are still considered incomplete, but please enjoy this peek at what we hope will be one of the core pillars of Crystal Horizons!

[i]Knight's Elemental Discharge skill, with much of the data for the skill available on the side.[/i]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44901040/3f25f65c66fcf0d2b06b689cdd89bb379b10fc89.png[/img]

[i]Additionally, Knight's Elemental Absorb passive, which powers Elemental Discharge among other skills. Has some related entries filled out for display purposes, although there will be more in the final product.[/i]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44901040/916a83e308aeb688bff24da209935a1dd2ecd830.png[/img]

notes.title: Weekly Update #48: Steam Page Launch & Beta Announcement!
notes.content:
Hey all! Finally, the Steam page is up and running! It's definitely been a long time coming! For this update, I want to lay out some details on something big coming in the near future!

For those of you wondering why this is update #48 and not #1, we've been doing these for a while over on our [url=https://discord.gg/jjhZcW5WqH]official Discord Server![/url] We're looking to archive these somewhere a bit more public in the future, but for now they are only available on the Discord.

So now that the Steam page is up, allow me to announce our next major goal. We're currently aiming to hold a Closed Beta Test sometime in the nearish future. I can't give a date right now, but I can share some details on what we're currently planning for it.

Currently, our plan for the beta build includes three playable maps, and eight playable classes. Upon starting the game, you will be prompted to select four units from the selection of eight we have. You will then run through each map with that party. Each map will have your party and the enemies at higher levels, so we can see how these classes perform at different level brackets.

Each class in Crystal Horizons features 10 mastery ranks, starting with approximately 25-35% of their total skillset, and unlocking the remainder as they gain more mastery ranks. This means a class should start with somewhat of an identity, and eventually flourish into the complex full concepts that we have spent so much time designing.

The first map in the beta will feature units at Character Level 1, at Mastery Rank 1 with their class. This represents the power level of the class at it's lowest. The second map will feature units at a higher Character Level and at Mastery Rank 5, giving us an idea of how a class plays at the midway point of mastery. Finally, our last map will feature a capped or near-cap Character Level, and Mastery Rank 10 classes. These will be the full kits, and should give us information on how a class plays once fully mastered, in endgame conditions.

Our goal with this structure is to gather as much data about the gameplay as possible, as well as confirm our formulas for stat growth over levels are delivering the intended experience. We aim to see which classes synergize with others, which classes are overperforming or underperforming, and what problems there are with both class design and map design. We plan to implement Unity Analytics for raw data, as well as provide a survey for players of the build.

During the beta period, you will be able to play through the set of maps as many times as you please. Currently we plan to restrict class stacking, allowing only one of each class to be selected, but are considering allowing players who have beaten the build once to stack classes however they please.

The classes present in the build will be Knight, Lumimancer, Pyromancer, Archer, Thief, Enchanter, Stormcaller and Berserker. We have locked in their skillsets for the time being, and expect there will be no further changes made to the concept while we implement their skillsets.

So, that's the news I have for you this week! We've got this update, as well as the previous 47, on the official Discord! Thanks for tuning in, and I'll see you all next week!
